### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.1

### Steps to reproduce

This is the counterpart of ticket #4860 but applied to open5gs-upfd instead of open5gs-smfd.

Apparently open5gs-upfd is not currently deleting session when the SMF is considered in failure (due to eg. Heartbeat timeout).

How to reproduce: Create some sessions on the UPF, then eg. kill the open5gs-smfd process, let UPF send Heartbeats until t3_holding_duration triggers.

### Logs

```shell

```

### Expected behaviour

As per TS 23.527 V18.6.0 clause 4.4.3.1:
> the UPF shall delete all the session contexts affected by the peer PFCP entity failure that it may have stored.

### Observed Behaviour

No session is deleted then according to open5gs-upfd logs.

This is well described by @MrBrownieCGN in https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/issues/4860#issuecomment-6202375701 point 5:

> 5. UPF side (re "this same issue also probably affects open5gs-upfd")
> 
> On main, when the UPF loses the heartbeat towards the SMF it only goes back to will_associate and keeps all
> sessions (src/upf/pfcp-sm.c:342-345); sessions of that SMF are removed only when the SMF comes back with a new
> Recovery Time Stamp (pfcp_restoration(), :371-386). Here the spec is not implementation specific. TS 23.527 V18.6.0,
> clause 4.4.3.1:
> 
> >    When a UPF detects that a peer PFCP entity in the SMF is not reachable for a preconfigured time, and the MPAS or SSET
> >    procedure specified for SMF set in clause 5.22 of 3GPP TS 29.244 [4]) are not used, the UPF shall delete all the
>>     session contexts affected by the peer PFCP entity failure that it may have stored.
> 
> The "preconfigured time" can reasonably be longer than the heartbeat give-up, but some bound seems to be required.
>

### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0 (master)

### Steps to reproduce

TTCN-3 test SMF_Tests.TC_pfcp_heartbeat_timeout from osmo-ttcn3-hacks.git showcases the scenario:
https://gerrit.osmocom.org/c/osmo-ttcn3-hacks/+/43873

### Logs

```shell
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: [2] LOCAL  Response Timeout for step 1 type 1 peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:623)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] WARNING: [2] LOCAL  No Reponse. Give up! for step 1 type 1 peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:642)

10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] DEBUG: smf_state_operational(): SMF_EVT_N4_NO_HEARTBEAT (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/smf-sm.c:94)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] DEBUG: smf_pfcp_state_associated(): SMF_EVT_N4_NO_HEARTBEAT (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:182)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] WARNING: No Heartbeat from UPF [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:426)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] ERROR: No UPF available (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:528)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] DEBUG: smf_pfcp_state_associated(): EXIT (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:182)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] INFO: PFCP de-associated [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:205)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] DEBUG: smf_pfcp_state_will_associate(): ENTRY (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:74)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: [4] LOCAL  Create  peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:131)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: Association Setup Request (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/build.c:87)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: [4] LOCAL  UPD TX-5  peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:231)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: [4] LOCAL  Commit  peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:500)
```

### Expected behaviour

As of current main  (d5d735c67356ff4cb2d86be6effadcc351b5b7b5), open5gs-smfd doesn't release UE sessions after the only UPF available is considered to be unavailable after obtaining no answer for a while (eg. multiple Heartbeat Requests not answered).

With current implementation, open5gs-smfd will keep trying forever until the UPF is available again and it sends a newer (bigger) Recovery timestamp which starts restoration value. 

The problem with that is that it may take a long time, or even "forever", for the UPF to become available again, and during that potentially long time the Control Plane assumes the user plane is working just fine, because the sessions are still active, which is false. This means for instance time accounting may go on on the OCS, etc.

Instead, when a Heartbeat timeout happens (configurable by the user, eg. 60 seconds) and the UPF is considered unavailable, it should release all the sessions on the core network so that the subscriber can see it has no PDU session instead of simply seeing no traffic passing through.

What do the specs say about this scenario? Well, they basically say it's "implementation specific".

3GPP TS 29.244 5.8.2 Behaviour with an Established PFCP Association
> When a PFCP Association is established with a UP function, the CP function:
> ...
> - shall check the responsiveness of the UP function using the Heartbeat procedure as specified in clause 6.2.2;

3GPP TS 23.527 4.2 N4 Failure and Restart Detection:
> Across PFCP based interfaces, an SMF and UPF shall utilize the PFCP Heartbeat Request and Heartbeat Response
> messages to detect a peer PFCP entity failure or restart as described in clause 19A of 3GPP TS 23.007

3GPP TS 23.527 4.5 N4 path failure:
> If the N4 path to the UPF is down, the SMF should handle this as an UPF Failure without Restart, see clause 4.3.3.

4.3.3 Restoration Procedure for PSA UPF Failure without Restart
> Procedures for PSA UPF failure without restart are implementation specific.

### Observed Behaviour

See "Expected behaviour" section.

items.title: PCF accepts evSubsc and reqAnis in app-session create but never reports the events
items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0-205-g2c80f8f (tested); main 51ee7ca (2026-10-26) has no `ev_subsc`/`req_anis` handling in `src/pcf`

### Steps to reproduce

1. A P-CSCF (AF) creates an app-session with an event subscription and a request for access-network information, e.g.
   ```json
   {"ascReqData": {"afAppId": "IMS Services", "ueIpv4": "10.45.0.2", "notifUri": "http://pcscf/n5/1",
     "medComponents": {...},
     "evSubsc": {"events": [{"event": "QOS_NOTIF"}, {"event": "ACCESS_TYPE_CHANGE"},
                             {"event": "ANI_REPORT"}, {"event": "FAILED_RESOURCES_ALLOCATION"}],
                 "reqAnis": ["USER_LOCATION", "UE_TIME_ZONE"],
                 "notifUri": "http://pcscf/n5/1"}}}
   ```
2. The PCF answers 201 Created.
3. Trigger the events: release the dedicated QoS flow / move the UE, or simply observe the create response.

### Logs

PCF answers 201 with no `evsNotif`; no `POST {notifUri}/notify` is ever sent. Captures available on request.

### Expected behaviour

TS 29.514 clause 4.2.2: events the PCF can report at once (e.g. ACCESS_TYPE_CHANGE with accessType/ratType, ANI_REPORT with ueLoc/ueTimeZone when reqAnis is present) are returned in `evsNotif` of the 201; later events are notified with `POST {notifUri}/notify` (clause 4.2.5.2). If an event is not supported, the PCF should not silently accept the subscription.

### Observed Behaviour

The subscription is accepted and ignored: `evSubsc` and `reqAnis` are not read anywhere in `src/pcf` (create handler `src/pcf/npcf-handler.c`), so the AF believes it is subscribed. For IMS this means the P-CSCF never learns of bearer loss (QOS_NOTIF) or the UE's location (NPLI for emergency/lawful-intercept use) although every answer was 201. Only `{notifUri}/terminate` is sent, on SM-policy deletion.

Related: #1120 (response event values, fixed), #4899 (signalling-path subscription).

### eNodeB/gNodeB

UERANSIM v3.3.0-37-g48554b7 (gNB)

### UE Models and versions

UERANSIM v3.3.0-37-g48554b7 (UE)

items.title: [Bug]: HSS Diameter listener goes down on an S6a request (ULR/AIR/PUR) whose Session-Id contains a NUL byte

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

labels.name: not-an-open5gs-bug
labels.description: This is not a bug in open5gs

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0

### Steps to reproduce

Sending the HSS a single S6a request (PUR/AIR/ULR) that is completely valid except that its Session-Id AVP (code 263) value contains a NUL (0x00) byte permanently breaks the HSS's Diameter interface. The `open5gs-hssd` process does not crash or exit, it keeps running, but it stops listening on TCP port 3868, so no peer can connect or be served anymore. 

Environment:
- open5gs v2.8.0
- HSS S6a listening on TCP 3868.

Steps:
1. Bring up the HSS normally.
2. From a Diameter peer the HSS accepts (an MME identity in the same realm),
   complete the CER/CEA handshake.
3. Send a well-formed S6a Update-Location-Request (command 316) in which the
   Session-Id AVP (code 263) value contains a NUL byte - e.g. take a normal
   Session-Id like `mme1.epc.mnc000.mcc460.3gppnetwork.org;1;1` and prepend
   four 0x00 bytes. Every other AVP is valid.
4. The HSS logs the fd_sess_new / fd_os_is_valid_os0 error cascade (see Logs)
   and stops listening on 3868. `open5gs-hssd` is still running.
The offending Session-Id AVP on the wire (code 263, M-bit set, length 0x3a; note
the four leading 0x00 bytes of the value, then the ASCII Session-Id):
    00 00 01 07 40 00 00 3a 00 00 00 00 61 74 74 61   ....@..:....mme
    63 6b 65 72 2e 65 70 63 2e 6d 6e 63 ...           cker.epc.mnc ...
Notes:
- It is NOT specific to ULR. The Session-Id is validated in `fd_msg_sess_get`
  during dispatch, *before* any command-specific handler runs, so AIR (318),
  PUR (321), any S6a request carrying a NUL-containing Session-Id, hit the
  exact same fault.

### Logs

```shell
ERROR: pid:Dispatch in fd_sess_new@sessions.c:405: ERROR: Invalid parameter '(fd_os_is_valid_os0(opt, optlen))', 22
ERROR: pid:Dispatch in fd_sess_fromsid_msg@sessions.c:556: ERROR: in '((ret))' : Invalid argument
ERROR: pid:Dispatch in fd_msg_sess_get@messages.c:1522: ERROR: in '((fd_sess_fromsid_msg(avp->avp_public.avp_value->os.data, avp->avp_public.avp_value->os.len, &msg->msg_sess, new)))' : Invalid argument
ERROR: pid:Dispatch in msg_dispatch@routing_dispatch.c:507: ERROR: in '((fd_msg_sess_get(fd_g_config->cnf_dict, msgptr, &sess, ((void *)0))))' : Invalid argument
ERROR: pid:Dispatch in process_thr@routing_dispatch.c:1119: ERROR: in '((*action_cb)(msg))' : Invalid argument


After these lines the HSS writes nothing more, TCP/3868 refuses connections
(connect → ECONNREFUSED), and `open5gs-hssd` is still alive.
```

### Expected behaviour

An invalid Session-Id is a per-message data error from one peer. The HSS should reject just that one request (e.g. with DIAMETER_INVALID_AVP_VALUE) or drop it, and keep serving every other peer and request. A single malformed request must never take down the whole S6a listener.

### Observed Behaviour

A single request with a NUL byte in the Session-Id makes the freeDiameter
Dispatch thread treat a routine per-message validation error as an
"unrecoverable error" and shut down the entire Diameter core.

Root cause, traced through open5gs/freeDiameter r1.5.0 (matches the log above
line-for-line):

1. `fd_os_is_valid_os0()` rejects any octet string containing a NUL byte
   (libfdproto.h):
   ```c
   static __inline__ int fd_os_is_valid_os0(uint8_t * os, size_t oslen) {
       /* not valid when it contains a \0 inside the octet string */
       return (memchr(os, '\0', oslen) == NULL);
   }
   ```
2. `fd_sess_new()` validates the Session-Id with it and returns EINVAL on failure
   (libfdproto/sessions.c:405):
   ```c
   CHECK_PARAMS( fd_os_is_valid_os0(opt, optlen) );
   ```
3. The EINVAL propagates up: `fd_sess_fromsid_msg` (sessions.c:556) →
   `fd_msg_sess_get` (messages.c:1522) → `msg_dispatch` (routing_dispatch.c:507):
   ```c
   CHECK_FCT( fd_msg_sess_get(fd_g_config->cnf_dict, msgptr, &sess, NULL) );
   ```
4. In the dispatch loop, ANY non-zero return from `msg_dispatch` is treated as
   fatal (routing_dispatch.c:1119):
   ```c
   CHECK_FCT_DO( (*action_cb)(msg), goto fatal_error);
   ...
   fatal_error:
       TRACE_DEBUG(INFO, "An unrecoverable error occurred, %s thread is terminating...", action_name);
       CHECK_FCT_DO(fd_core_shutdown(), );
   ```

So a bad Session-Id in one inbound message triggers `fd_core_shutdown()`: the Diameter core stops listening on 3868. But `open5gs-hssd` does not exit, so no restart policy fires and the HSS is down until manually restarted.


### eNodeB/gNodeB

N/A

### UE Models and versions

N/A

items.title: SMF aborts on two QoS rules for the same QFI in one PDU Session Modification Request

labels.name: status:already-fixed
labels.description: This issue has already been fixed in the codebase or addressed in a previous issue.

items.body:
## Symptom

`ogs_assert_if_reached()` in `gsm_handle_pdu_session_modification_request()` terminates
the SMF process. `ogs_assert_if_reached()` is `ogs_fatal()` + `ogs_abort()`, so every PDU
session of every other subscriber goes down with it. The flag combination that reaches it
is decoded from the QoS rules IE the UE sent, so a single malformed NAS message from one
subscriber is enough. No timing or race is involved.

This is the same assertion that #4672 reached through the QoS flow descriptions IE.
`72913dc92` closed that route. The QoS rules IE reaches it without any help from the QoS
flow descriptions handler, and that route is still open on current main.

## Reproducer

- Open5GS commit: bb810d384
- Config: stock 5GC, one subscriber with one active PDU session and one QoS flow.
- Trigger: after the session is established, send one PDU SESSION MODIFICATION REQUEST
  whose QoS rules IE (TS 24.501 9.11.4.13) carries two rules naming the **same existing**
  QFI X:

  | rule | operation code | QFI | packet filters |
  |------|----------------|-----|----------------|
  | 1 | 2 — delete existing QoS rule | X | none |
  | 2 | 1 — create new QoS rule | X | >= 1 |

  Both orders of the two rules reach the assertion.

- Expected: the request is answered, the SMF stays up.
- Actual:

```
[gsm] INFO : Requested QoS rule [code:2 id:1 num_of_packet_filter:0]  gsm-handler.c:245
[gsm] INFO : Requested QoS rule [code:1 id:1 num_of_packet_filter:1]  gsm-handler.c:245
[gsm] ERROR: Invalid modification request
             [REMOVE combined with TFT/QOS-MODIFY pfcp_flags:0x480]   gsm-handler.c:607
[gsm] FATAL: gsm_handle_pdu_session_modification_request:
             should not be reached.                                   gsm-handler.c:611
[core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 10 addresses                       ogs-abort.c:37
```

  The SMF process is gone at this point.

## Root cause analysis

Rule 1 (delete) sets `OGS_PFCP_MODIFY_REMOVE` and puts the QoS flow on
`sess->qos_flow_to_modify_list`. Rule 2 (create) sets `OGS_PFCP_MODIFY_TFT_NEW` for the
same QFI; `qos_flow_find_or_add()` does not add a second list entry for a flow already on
the list. The list therefore still holds exactly one element and passes the
`ogs_list_count(&sess->qos_flow_to_modify_list) != 1` check at gsm-handler.c:585.

`pfcp_flags` is now `REMOVE|TFT_NEW`, which is exactly the combination the block at
gsm-handler.c:592 was written to catch — and it catches it with `ogs_assert_if_reached()`.

`pfcp_flags` here is not an internal invariant. It is derived entirely from the QoS rules
IE (9.11.4.13) and the QoS flow descriptions IE (9.11.4.12) of the UE's request, so every
combination reachable at that point is remote input.

The comment directly above the check already says what should happen instead:

> pfcp_flags is derived from the content of the UE's PDU Session Modification Request, so
> a misbehaving UE can request a removal combined with a TFT/QoS modification for the same
> QoS flow. This is invalid input, not an internal error: log the exact flag combination
> and reject the request instead of aborting the SMF.

The log line is there; the rejection is not.

## Spec reference

TS 24.501 V18.13.0 §6.4.2.4.1 — "UE-requested PDU session modification procedure not
accepted by the network", General:

> Upon receipt of a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION REQUEST message, if the SMF does not accepts
> the request to modify the PDU session, the SMF shall create a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION
> REJECT message.

and, further down the same clause:

> The SMF shall send the PDU SESSION MODIFICATION REJECT message.

The clause lists the cause values it expects there, among them `#95 - 111 protocol
errors`, which covers the `#96 "invalid mandatory information"` that the existing
`cleanup:` path already uses. The message itself is defined in §8.3.8, the QoS rules IE
and its operation codes in §9.11.4.13.

## Suggested fix (optional)

The function already has a rejection path: `cleanup:` at gsm-handler.c:642 builds a
PDU SESSION MODIFICATION REJECT and returns `OGS_ERROR`, and every other unacceptable
request in this function goes there. Replacing the `ogs_assert_if_reached()` with a jump
to that path would make the code do what its comment describes. Which 5GSM cause fits best
is your call — the existing path uses `OGS_5GSM_CAUSE_INVALID_MANDATORY_INFORMATION`.

The other `ogs_assert_if_reached()` in the QoS rules loop of this file looks unreachable
from UE input: its enclosing else-if already restricts the operation code to the three
values the chain covers. It seems fine as a defensive invariant.

## Related

- #4672 — same assertion, reached through the QoS flow descriptions IE; fixed by 72913dc92.
  This report is the remaining route into the same assertion.
- #4512 / #4429 — same message shape, reported earlier; 884747c30 fixed the packet-filter
  index handling in `reconfigure_packet_filter()`, which is a different defect in the same
  request.

items.title: [Bug]: SMF cancels the UDM deregistration of a released PDU session when an unrelated HTTP/2 stream closes, the session stays in will_deregister

labels.name: type:bug
labels.description: Open5GS bug

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0 and main (d5d735c6)

### Steps to reproduce

Hi,

I'm testing a gNB/UE simulator I'm writing against Open5GS (all NFs from Open5GS with the SCP, on one host), and one of my scenarios sometimes leaves a PDU session stuck in the SMF:

- Start a fresh core and register one UE
- Establish PDU sessions 5 and 6
- The UE releases session 6 (PDU Session Release Request / Command / Complete)
- 1 ms after the PDU Session Release Complete, the gNB sends a UE Context Release Request (user inactivity), so the AMF deactivates session 5 (`sm-contexts/1/modify` with `upCnxState` DEACTIVATED)

It does not happen on every run: 16 runs out of 30 on main and 6 out of 30 on v2.8.0, with a freshly started core each time.

### Logs

```shell
# SMF on main, debug level, only the lines of the release of session 6 and of the modify of session 5
10/12 10:00:08.973: [smf] DEBUG: smf_gsm_state_5gc_session_will_deregister(): ENTRY (../src/smf/gsm-sm.c:4122)
10/12 10:00:08.974: [sbi] DEBUG: [204:POST] http://127.0.0.200:7777/npcf-smpolicycontrol/v1/sm-policies/2/delete (../lib/sbi/client.c:744)
10/12 10:00:08.974: [smf] DEBUG: smf_gsm_state_5gc_session_will_deregister(): OGS_EVENT_NAME_SBI_CLIENT (../src/smf/gsm-sm.c:4122)
10/12 10:00:08.974: [sbi] DEBUG: [DELETE] http://127.0.0.200:7777/nudm-sdm/v2/imsi-208930000000001/sdm-subscriptions/f17054be-c612-41f1-a88a-cf0e238cf1df (../lib/sbi/client.c:797)
10/12 10:00:08.974: [sbi] DEBUG: STREAM added [21] (../lib/sbi/nghttp2-server.c:1777)
10/12 10:00:08.974: [sbi] DEBUG: [POST] /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts/1/modify (../lib/sbi/nghttp2-server.c:1312)
10/12 10:00:08.975: [sbi] DEBUG: [204:DELETE] http://127.0.0.200:7777/nudm-sdm/v2/imsi-208930000000001/sdm-subscriptions/f17054be-c612-41f1-a88a-cf0e238cf1df (../lib/sbi/client.c:744)
10/12 10:00:08.975: [smf] DEBUG: smf_gsm_state_5gc_session_will_deregister(): OGS_EVENT_NAME_SBI_CLIENT (../src/smf/gsm-sm.c:4122)
10/12 10:00:08.975: [sbi] DEBUG: [DELETE] http://127.0.0.200:7777/nudm-uecm/v1/imsi-208930000000001/registrations/smf-registrations/6 (../lib/sbi/client.c:797)
10/12 10:00:08.975: [sbi] DEBUG: {"upCnxState":"DEACTIVATED"} (../lib/sbi/nghttp2-server.c:715)
10/12 10:00:08.975: [sbi] DEBUG: STREAM closed [21] (../lib/sbi/nghttp2-server.c:1435)
10/12 10:00:08.975: [sbi] ERROR: Canceling pending outbound SBI transaction on HTTP/2 stream close [xact:13,stream:21,service:nudm-uecm] (../lib/sbi/nghttp2-server.c:866)
10/12 10:00:08.976: [sbi] DEBUG: [204:DELETE] http://127.0.0.200:7777/nudm-uecm/v1/imsi-208930000000001/registrations/smf-registrations/6 (../lib/sbi/client.c:744)
10/12 10:00:08.976: [smf] ERROR: SBI transaction has already been removed [13] (../src/smf/smf-sm.c:1041)
```

### Expected behaviour

The release of session 6 completes and the SMF sends the `sm-context-status` notification for it to the AMF.

### Observed Behaviour

The DELETE to `nudm-uecm` for session 6 is cancelled when stream 21 closes, and stream 21 is the modify of session 5, which has nothing to do with it. The 204 from the UDM then finds no transaction, no `sm-context-status/6` is sent, and session 6 stays in `smf_gsm_state_5gc_session_will_deregister`. It was still there after the UE deregistered, and only went away when the same UE created PDU session 6 again.

On v2.8.0 the UE sees it: when it registers again afterwards, the AMF logs `known UE by SUCI` and never sends an Authentication Request (6 times out of the 6 where the cancel happened, I waited 10 s). On main the UE is authenticated again, but the session is stuck in the SMF all the same.

I had a look at the code (line numbers are for d5d735c6), here is what I think happens:

- `gsm-sm.c:3856` (and `3956`) starts this clean-up with `smf_sbi_cleanup_session(sess, NULL, SMF_UECM_STATE_DEREG_BY_N1N2, ...)`, so its transactions have no stream.
- When a response comes back, `e->h.sbi.data` holds the transaction id (`smf-sm.c:992`), and `smf-sm.c:1009-1011` replaces it with the stream id only if `assoc_stream_id` is valid. Here it is not, so the session FSM is called with the transaction id still in there.
- `smf_gsm_state_5gc_session_will_deregister` reads that value as a stream id (`gsm-sm.c:4201-4203`) and looks it up with `ogs_sbi_stream_find_by_id()`. If a stream with that pool id exists at that moment, it is passed to `smf_sbi_cleanup_session(sess, stream, ...)` at `gsm-sm.c:4296`, and the next request, the UECM deregistration, gets attached to it.
- When that stream closes, `stream_remove_xact_all()` in `nghttp2-server.c` (from #4578) cancels the request.

In my runs the SDM unsubscribe of session 6 is transaction 12, and the modify of session 5 is the 12th stream of the SMF (4 NF status notifications, then the requests of the two sessions), so the two ids are the same. With gdb at `nghttp2-server.c:866` I see the closing stream with pool id 12 (HTTP/2 stream 21, `POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts/1/modify`) and the cancelled transaction 13 with `assoc_stream_id` 12.

As a test I added `else e->h.sbi.data = OGS_UINT_TO_POINTER(OGS_INVALID_POOL_ID);` after `smf-sm.c:1011`, and it did not happen any more (0 out of 30). I don't know if that is the right fix, other states read `e->h.sbi.data` the same way.

It needs the two ids to line up, which with my scenario happens on a freshly started SMF. I don't know how often that can be on an SMF that has been running for a while, so it may be rare outside of a test like this one. I have the debug logs of all the NFs for these runs if you want them.

Thanks a lot!
Valentin

items.title: [Security Bug]: AMF accepts NGAP PathSwitchRequest without ownership check + Crashes due to race condition

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0 (main @ `ee596937d`, v2.8.0-76). 
Still unfixed on current main (source-checked 2026-09-04 @ `941e4cc2d`).

### Security impact

Any associated peer can re-home a live UE's NGAP context and redirect
its downlink FAR to an attacker-chosen endpoint due to a lack of ownership in the
referenced UE context. The redirection of the victim's downlink stream to 
an attacker-controlled endpoint is the confidentiality/integrity impact, and the controlled 
outage is the availability impact.

**Update: The same primitive can also be used to trigger AMF process abort with no SMF 
precondition due to race condition**

**CVSS v3.1 Score: 8.8 (High)** - AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

### Affected components

The **AMF** — NGAP PathSwitchRequest handling
(`src/amf/ngap-handler.c`, `ngap_handle_path_switch_request()`) and the
UE-context/`ran_ue` management it drives.

### Summary

`ngap_handle_path_switch_request()` resolves the target UE with a global
lookup by the AMF_UE_NGAP_ID carried in the message
(`ran_ue_find_by_amf_ue_ngap_id()`, `src/amf/ngap-handler.c:3074`) and
never verifies that the sending NGAP association is the one that
currently owns (serves) that UE context. Any associated gNB, including
a rogue gNB smuggled out of a UE data plane, can re-home a
live peer UE's NGAP context to itself by knowing or enumerating the
peer's AMF_UE_NGAP_ID. After acceptance, the AMF runs its normal 
path-switch chain: the context move is logged
([OLD]/[NEW] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID), the handler's PDU-session loop sends an
N11 SM-context update, and the SMF/UPF rewrite the victim's downlink
FAR toward the attacker's endpoint (UPF `gtp_connect() [10.45.0.9]:2152`). 
The victim's downlink was measurably cut and recovered only
when the victim re-registered (a full re-registration on a new address).

This bug can also be used to trigger a race condition assert.
1. The PathSwitchRequest handler switches the victim's context to the
   sender's gNB with no ownership check
   (`ran_ue->gnb_id = gnb->id`).
2. When that association goes down, `amf_gnb_remove()` frees the
   `amf_gnb_t` while the per-UE deactivation chain (N11/PFCP for the
   victim's live PDU sessions) is still in flight. The `ran_ue` is not
   reaped (the sweep skips it because the deactivation created new SBI
   transactions) but keeps pointing at the freed gNB.
3. A PathSwitchRequest re-claim for the victim's AMF_UE_NGAP_ID
   arriving inside that window (delta ≈ 0–1 ms observed) resolves the
   still-alive context, then `ran_ue_switch_to_gnb()` resolves the
   dangling `gnb_id` → `amf_gnb_find_by_id()` returns NULL →
   `ogs_assert(gnb)` aborts `open5gs-amfd`
   (`src/amf/context.c:1451`). amfd is left `<defunct>`; every NGAP
   service is lost until the open5gs containers restart.

These issues are still present on current main (`1f70b24c`).
The RAN-node-ownership enforcement commit `9a22baa76`
("Enforce RAN node ownership in handover handlers") adds
`source_ue->gnb_id != gnb->id` checks to the NGAP/S1AP handover handlers
but its own commit message explicitly excludes PathSwitchRequest.

### Steps to reproduce
#### Issue A: PathSwitchRequest from any peer.
Lab: Two attached UEs.
* Attacker UE `10.45.0.9`
* Benign peer UE `10.45.0.8`
* Core container `192.168.233.132` hosting both AMF (NGAP SCTP 38412) and UPF (GTP-U 2152).

1. Attach both UEs.
2. From the attacker UE, open an SCTP association to
   `192.168.233.132:38412` with inner IP packets sent as ordinary uplink
   IP packets through the attacker's established PDU session (the UPF
   decapsulates and the kernel delivers them to the AMF, as in the PFCP
   smuggling path). AMF log: `gNB-N2 accepted[10.45.0.9]:33250 in
   ng-path module`.
3. Complete NG Setup with a gNB ID distinct from the real gNB (fake gNB
   ID 2) and the lab PLMN/TAC (001/01, TAC 1) — NGSetupResponse,
   successfulOutcome (proc 21), 54 bytes.
4. Probe PathSwitchRequest candidates (attacker-chosen RAN_UE_NGAP_ID
   5000, UserLocationInformation with the lab TAC): ErrorIndication-sweep
   the 60 unknown AMF_UE_NGAP_IDs (3–7, 10–64, PDU Session ID 1), then
   send three probes each (PDU Session IDs 1, 2, 3) to the two live IDs
   — the peer's (8) and the attacker's own (9). Record per-candidate
   responses.
5. The peer's live ID 8 with session 1 is accepted: verify the
   `[OLD]`/`[NEW]` context move in the AMF log, the UPF Session
   Modification with `gtp_connect() [10.45.0.9]:2152` two milliseconds
   later, and re-measure the peer's downlink. The attacker's own ID 9 is
   likewise accepted (context re-homed, UPF session modified) but its
   probes draw no decodable response.

#### Issue B: Crash AMF
Lab: Two attached UEs.
* Attacker UE (PDU-session address `10.45.0.2`
* Benign peer UE `imsi-001010123456790` with a live PDU session.
* Core container `192.168.233.132` hosting AMF (NGAP SCTP 38412) and UPF (GTP-U 2152).
Script: `r8b_race.py` (attached zip; staged in the attacker UE container with
the `ueprobe` package and `pycrate`); the associations are smuggled as
ordinary uplink IP packets through the attacker's PDU session.

1. Attach both UEs (the peer's live session is what keeps its `ran_ue`
   alive through the removal).
2. From the attacker UE open association B (NG Setup, gNB ID 3), then
   association A (NG Setup, gNB ID 2). Both get NGSetupResponse
   (successfulOutcome, proc 21).
3. Re-home the peer's context onto A: PathSwitchRequest from A
   (attacker-chosen `RAN_UE_NGAP_ID` 5000, the peer's live
   `AMF_UE_NGAP_ID`, UserLocationInformation with the lab TAC) →
   PathSwitchRequestAcknowledge (proc 25).
4. SHUTDOWN A and, delta = 0, send the re-claim PathSwitchRequest for
   the peer's ID from B (single burst pre-associated, no handshake
   inside the window). The script sweeps delta 0–40 ms in 0.4 ms steps
   for robustness.
5. Detect: no response to the re-claim and a fresh NG Setup that gets
   no answer, meaning that amfd is gone. The script's liveness check is a full NG
   Setup exchange (a raw-SCTP connect alone cannot see a dead peer).

### Logs (Attached)
#### Issue A: PathSwitchRequest from any peer.
[R8-amf-pathswitch-context-hijack.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31734861/R8-amf-pathswitch-context-hijack.zip)

```shell
[amf] INFO: gNB-N2 accepted[10.45.0.9]:33250 in ng-path module
[amf] INFO: PathSwitchRequest
[amf] ERROR: No RAN UE Context : AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[3]    (x60: ids 3..7 and 10..64, cause radioNetwork=14)
[amf] INFO:     [OLD] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[8] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[8]     (14:33:27.685 — peer's live ID)
[amf] INFO:     [NEW] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[5000] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[8]
[upf] DEBUG: Session Modification Request                     (14:33:27.687)
[gtp] INFO: gtp_connect() [10.45.0.9]:2152                    (14:33:27.687)
[amf] INFO:     [OLD] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[9] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[9]     (14:33:27.851 — attacker's own ID)
[amf] INFO:     [NEW] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[5000] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[9]
[upf] DEBUG: Session Modification Request                     (14:33:27.852)
```

(all lines from `q023_amf.log` and `q023_upf.log`. `q023_smf.log`'s
capture starts at 14:33:28.167, so the N11 SM-context update has no
SMF-side line; the only `POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts/7/modify`
in it is at 14:34:05.777 — the association-release-phase modify for the
victim's session, after which the downlink stayed cut.)

(Each accepted path switch also logs `UE Security Capability mismatch in PathSwitchRequest`.
Per TS 33.501 6.7.3.1 comment in the handler, the AMF answers a mismatched
PathSwitchRequest with its locally stored UE security capabilities in
the PathSwitchRequestAcknowledge (`ngap-handler.c:3310-3314`).)

58 diverted GTP-U datagrams were captured on
the attacker's UDP 2152 listener (`q023_sink.jsonl`), all on the
attacker's own-session TEID 0xa5000091, none on the peer-session TEID
0xa5000081 (attacker-chosen and installed by the AMF in the victim's
downlink FAR).

#### Issue B: Crash AMF

[R8b-amf-pathswitch-context-hijack-crash.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31863769/R8b-amf-pathswitch-context-hijack-crash.zip)

Run 4 of 4 (11:09:06), verbatim from `amf.log`
(`amf-crash-r8b3-w4.log` in the zip; runs 1–3 in `amf-crash-r8b3-w1/2/3.log`):

    09/05 11:09:05.944: [amf] INFO: PathSwitchRequest (ngap-handler.c:3009)
    09/05 11:09:05.944: [amf] INFO:     [OLD] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[4] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[4]
    09/05 11:09:05.944: [amf] INFO:     [OLD] TAC[1] CellID[0x10] (ngap-handler.c:3104)
    09/05 11:09:05.944: [amf] INFO:     [NEW] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[5000] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[4]
    09/05 11:09:05.944: [amf] INFO:     [NEW] TAC[1] CellID[0x10] (ngap-handler.c:3306)
    09/05 11:09:06.495: [amf] INFO: gNB-N2[10.45.0.2] connection refused!!! (amf-sm.c:882)
    09/05 11:09:06.495: [amf] INFO: [Removed] Number of gNBs is now 2 (context.c:1305)
    09/05 11:09:06.495: [amf] INFO: PathSwitchRequest (ngap-handler.c:3009)
    09/05 11:09:06.495: [amf] INFO:     [OLD] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[5000] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[4]
    09/05 11:09:06.496: [amf] INFO:     [OLD] TAC[1] CellID[0x10]
    09/05 11:09:06.496: [amf] FATAL: ran_ue_switch_to_gnb: Assertion `gnb' failed. (../open5gs-src/src/amf/context.c:1451)
    09/05 11:09:06.496: [core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 11 addresses (../open5gs-src/lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)

Four consecutive runs, identical fingerprint, delta = 0 each time:

| run | re-home | `[Removed]` | re-claim → FATAL (`context.c:1451`) |
|-----|-----------------|--------------------|--------------------------------------|
| 1   | 10:55:58.825    | 10:55:59.376       | 10:55:59.377                         |
| 2   | 11:01:26.841    | 11:01:27.391       | 11:01:27.392                         |
| 3   | 11:06:44.628    | 11:06:45.179       | 11:06:45.180                         |
| 4   | 11:09:05.944    | 11:09:06.495       | 11:09:06.496                         |

After each abort `open5gs-amfd` is `<defunct>` (zombie; no child reaper
restarts it) meaning that we get no NGAP service until the open5gs containers restart.

### Expected behaviour

The AMF must verify that the NGAP association sending a
PathSwitchRequest is the association that currently owns (serves) the
referenced UE context, and reject otherwise (cause: unexpected NGAP peer
/ unknown local UE NGAP-ID) without leaking which AMF_UE_NGAP_IDs are
live. Additionally, the AMF must never resolve a UE context to a freed gNB. The association
close and the UE-context cleanup must be ordered so no `ran_ue` can
outlive the gNB it points at. A re-claim for a context the sender does not own
should additionally fail the ownership check before any switch.
**Upstream itself applied exactly this class of ownership check to
the neighbouring handlers in `9a22baa76`.**

### Observed Behaviour
#### Issue A: PathSwitchRequest from any peer.
```c
/* src/amf/ngap-handler.c @ ee596937d — ngap_handle_path_switch_request() */
ran_ue = ran_ue_find_by_amf_ue_ngap_id(amf_ue_ngap_id);        /* :3074 — global lookup */
if (!ran_ue) {
    ogs_error("No RAN UE Context : AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[%lld]",
            (long long)amf_ue_ngap_id);
    r = ngap_send_error_indication(
            gnb, (uint64_t *)RAN_UE_NGAP_ID, &amf_ue_ngap_id,
            NGAP_Cause_PR_radioNetwork,
            NGAP_CauseRadioNetwork_unknown_local_UE_NGAP_ID);
    return;
}
amf_ue = amf_ue_find_by_id(ran_ue->amf_ue_id);
…
/* Change ran_ue to the NEW gNB after mandatory IE validation */   /* :3288 */
ran_ue_switch_to_gnb(ran_ue, gnb);                                  /* :3289 */
ogs_info("    [NEW] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[%lld] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[%lld] ",    /* :3291 */
    (long long)ran_ue->ran_ue_ngap_id, (long long)ran_ue->amf_ue_ngap_id);
```

The lookup is global across all gNB associations: `gnb` (the sending
association) is never compared with the context's serving gNB. The
ErrorIndication branch at `:3074-3085` is the enumeration oracle — it
distinguishes "no such UE" from "accepted" on the same ID space. After
acceptance the handler logs the `[OLD]`/`[NEW]` move and proceeds into
the N11/N4 modification chain.

#### Issue B: Crash AMF
`ogs_assert(gnb)` fails in `ran_ue_switch_to_gnb()` (`context.c:1451`)
and amfd aborts as `<defunct>` zombie and we get no NGAP service until the
containers restart.

items.title: AMF/SMF stale UE context after gNB SCTP reconnection causes PDU session failure (HTTP 400)

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose

labels.name: not-an-open5gs-bug
labels.description: This is not a bug in open5gs

items.body:
**Description**

When a gNB disconnects and reconnects (e.g. during cell reconfiguration that requires lock/unlock), some UEs — particularly iPhone 17 Pro Max — end up in a state where they are registered but have no data connectivity. The SMF logs show repeated HTTP response error [400] when attempting N1N2 message transfer.

  **Environment**
  - Open5GS v2.7.6 on Ubuntu 22.04
  - Commercial 5G SA gNB (NR TDD, n77)
  - UE: iPhone 17 Pro Max with dual SIM (private 5G eSIM + commercial SIM)
  - iPhone 14 on the same cell does not exhibit this issue

  **Steps to Reproduce**
  1. gNB connected to Open5GS AMF via SCTP, UEs attached with active PDU sessions
  2. gNB performs cell reconfiguration (internally does lock/unlock, dropping SCTP association)
  3. SCTP association re-establishes, gNB sends NG Setup Request, AMF accepts
  4. iPhone re-registers (Registration complete logged in AMF)
  5. iPhone requests PDU session — SMF creates session and assigns IP
  6. SMF sends N1N2 message transfer to AMF — gets HTTP 400
  7. Session removed, iPhone retries every ~16 seconds, same failure
  8. iPhone shows "attached" but has no data connectivity

  **AMF/SMF Log**
```
  [gmm] INFO: [imsi-xxxx] Registration complete
  [gmm] INFO: UE SUPI[imsi-xxxx] DNN[internet] S_NSSAI[SST:1 SD:0xffffff] smContextRef[NULL]
  [smf] ERROR: [imsi-xxxx:1] HTTP response error [400]
  [amf] ERROR: No UE context [imsi-xxxx]
  [amf] ERROR: No RAN UE Context : AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[64]
```
  **Expected Behaviour**
When the SCTP association drops, the AMF should fully clean up all UE contexts (AMF-UE, RAN-UE, and associated SMF sessions). When the gNB reconnects and UEs re-register, they should get a completely fresh context with working PDU sessions.

  **Workaround**
Restarting open5gs-amfd and open5gs-smfd after the gNB reconnects clears the stale state and UEs connect successfully on the next attempt.

  **Additional Notes**
  - The issue is more pronounced with iPhone 17 Pro Max than iPhone 14
  - The gNB's SCTP disconnect/reconnect happens within seconds
  - UPF data path is confirmed working (ping from UPF to UE IP succeeds) but zero packets appear on ogstun from the affected UE

items.title: [Bug]: NRF crash on inter-PLMN `GET /nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances` when a delayed Home-NRF response arrives after the original client disconnects

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Steps to reproduce

### Description

NRF aborts during inter-PLMN discovery forwarding if the original HTTP/2 client
disconnects before the Home-NRF response comes back.

The forwarding path stores a raw `ogs_sbi_stream_t *` inside `nrf_assoc`:

```c
typedef struct nrf_assoc_s {
    ...
    ogs_sbi_stream_t *stream;
} nrf_assoc_t;
```

```c
assoc->stream = stream;
```

When the delayed Home-NRF response arrives, `discover_handler()` reuses that raw
pointer without checking whether the original stream/session is still alive:

```c
stream = assoc->stream;
ogs_assert(stream);
...
ogs_expect(true == ogs_sbi_server_send_response(stream, response));
```

But if the original client timed out and disconnected first, nghttp2 closes the
stream and frees it:

```c
stream = nghttp2_session_get_stream_user_data(session, stream_id);
...
stream_remove(stream);
```

The later response send then walks into `server_send_rspmem_persistent()` with
an invalid socket and aborts:

```c
fd = sock->fd;
ogs_assert(fd != INVALID_SOCKET);
```

This is a distinct crash from the already documented inter-PLMN `SearchResult`
pool-exhaustion issues. Here the attacker only needs a delayed but otherwise
valid Home-NRF response plus a client disconnect.

### Root cause

- Entry route:
  `GET /nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances`
- Preconditions:
  inter-PLMN forwarding path with `hnrf-uri`, and the original client must
  disconnect before the Home-NRF replies
- Raw association storage:
  `../src/nrf/context.h:44-48`
  and `../src/nrf/context.c:137-153`
- Response callback:
  `../src/nrf/nnrf-handler.c:1360-1405`
- Stream free on disconnect:
  `../lib/sbi/nghttp2-server.c:1306-1327`
- Exact crash site:
  `../lib/sbi/nghttp2-server.c:643`
- Root cause family:
  stale stream / use-after-free style response handling leading to assertion
  abort
- Controlling factor:
  delayed Home-NRF response timing relative to original client disconnect

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start a fake h2c Home-NRF on the Docker `open5gs` network:

```bash
printf 'control\n' > /home/ubuntu/open5gs_277/.audit_tmp/nrf_fake_hnrf.mode
docker run --rm -d \
  --name hnrfctl \
  --network open5gs \
  --network-alias hnrfctl \
  -e NRF_FAKE_PORT=80 \
  -v /home/ubuntu/open5gs_277/.audit_tmp:/srv \
  node:24-alpine \
  node /srv/nrf_fake_hnrf.js
```

2. Control case: restart the local NRF and issue the inter-PLMN request with an
   immediate Home-NRF response:

```bash
docker restart nrf
sleep 2

docker run --rm --network open5gs curlimages/curl:8.10.1 \
```

### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Steps to reproduce

### Description

NRF aborts during inter-PLMN discovery forwarding if the original HTTP/2 client
disconnects before the Home-NRF response comes back.

The forwarding path stores a raw `ogs_sbi_stream_t *` inside `nrf_assoc`:

```c
typedef struct nrf_assoc_s {
    ...
    ogs_sbi_stream_t *stream;
} nrf_assoc_t;
```

```c
assoc->stream = stream;
```

When the delayed Home-NRF response arrives, `discover_handler()` reuses that raw
pointer without checking whether the original stream/session is still alive:

```c
stream = assoc->stream;
ogs_assert(stream);
...
ogs_expect(true == ogs_sbi_server_send_response(stream, response));
```

But if the original client timed out and disconnected first, nghttp2 closes the
stream and frees it:

```c
stream = nghttp2_session_get_stream_user_data(session, stream_id);
...
stream_remove(stream);
```

The later response send then walks into `server_send_rspmem_persistent()` with
an invalid socket and aborts:

```c
fd = sock->fd;
ogs_assert(fd != INVALID_SOCKET);
```

This is a distinct crash from the already documented inter-PLMN `SearchResult`
pool-exhaustion issues. Here the attacker only needs a delayed but otherwise
valid Home-NRF response plus a client disconnect.

### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Description

AMF aborts if an SMF returns `200 OK` or `204 No Content` for:

```text
POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts/{smContextRef}/modify
```

but omits `SmContextUpdatedData.n2SmInfo` while the AMF is waiting for the
Service Request activation response.

The reachable live path is:

```text
UE Service Request with Uplink Data Status
  -> gmm_handle_service_request()
  -> amf_sbi_send_activating_session()
  -> POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts/{smContextRef}/modify
  -> amf_nsmf_pdusession_handle_update_sm_context()
```

`gmm_handle_service_request()` triggers that `/modify` transaction at
`../src/amf/gmm-handler.c:855-860`. When the success response comes back
without `n2SmInfo`, `amf_nsmf_pdusession_handle_update_sm_context()` falls into
the success/no-N2 branch and reaches the explicit “Not reached here” abort for

Hey @acetcom 

I've spent some time studying my SA attach issue, and have narrowed the problem down. It seems to be related to the session context...

Currently running tests with a Qualcomm x55 modem in SA mode. I get exactly the same results with the Huawei Balong 5000 in SA mode.

Fresh compile of git master; commit 22b09443ce41c34786df167916d603bd17771d69. I cleaned out MongoDB and recreated the USIM profiles.

Running all Open5GS components on the Amarisoft gNB computer, so all NFs using the default IP addresses. gNB is on `127.0.1.1`
____

### Clean Restart

- Completely restart the entire core network; ie power cycle all 5GC control plane functions + the UPF.
- Attach gNB
- Attach UE

Result = attach works first time
PCAP and all debug log files = [SA_restartAll.zip](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/files/6160460/SA_restartAll.zip)


After this initial successful attach,
* I can powercycle the UE and it reattaches successfully
* I can powercycle the gNB; after it does NGsetup, UE reattaches successfully

____

### Control Plane Restart

- Ok, so this time we assume something has happened with the control plane daemons, and they have restarted
- The UPF remains running (from the above test) - does not get restarted
- After the SMF comes back online, it re- PFCP associates with the UPF
- Attach gNB
- Attach UE

Result = attach fails
PCAP and all debug log files = [SA_restartAll_exceptUPF.zip](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/files/6160461/SA_restartAll_exceptUPF.zip)

After the UE sends `UplinkNASTransport`, SMF sends UPF a `PFCP Session Deletion Request` message. UPF responds with session context errors, then the control plane seems to stop doing anything, leading to the gNB timing out after 10 seconds and kicking the UE. The UE then goes into a cycle of failed attach requests.

This is totally repeatable, and occurs with both the Qualcomm and Huawei UEs. 

____

Not sure what you make of this? Is this expected behaviour?

Cheers
Kenny
